current.text: He signed with Chicago on a two-year deal with a team option in the second year.
He is in the projected Bulls starting five with Josh Giddey, Matas Buzelis, Caleb Wilson and Nick Claxton. He is the team's main off-ball shooter, and the roster lacks shooting.
Nikola Vucevic and Coby White are gone. Giddey, Buzelis and Wilson are expected to have lower usage than Powell.
Experts expect him to lead the Bulls in usage, in the high 20s, all season unless he is traded. Nobody is coming in to take his usage.
He is 33. He ranked 73rd in category leagues last season.
Over the last two to three months of last season he shot 33% from three, his free throws fell below 80%, and he dropped outside the top 150.
Experts value him around 80th overall, a round 7 to 8 pick. One expert would take him in the 70s or 80s, with a best case of 40th and a worst case of 136th.
His ESPN rank of 64 is a bit high. He has more downside than upside.

The Bulls front office signs older players and hopes to trade them, and Powell's short contract makes him easy to trade. If he goes to a team where he is the third option, his fantasy value collapses.
With a March 28 end, the Bulls play 10 games in fantasy playoff weeks 19 to 21 (3-3-4). They have 15 back-to-backs, and their overall schedule is average.

durable.text: He is a points and threes player with decent efficiency. He adds little else.
He adds little in rebounds, assists and blocks.
He is good at getting to the free throw line and shoots about 82% there.

His value depends entirely on high usage. He puts up big numbers when he has the ball to himself and fades when he shares it with a good player. Without big usage he is useless for fantasy, even when he shoots around 40% from three.
His value depends on his shooting. An off shooting year hurts his value badly.
He is not a point guard and cannot dribble well.
Hayes says scoring over 20 points on about 15 shots per game is not tremendous fantasy value.

note: Experts put him around 80th (round 7 to 8). That fits his Yahoo rank of 87 and 9 USD value, and our league paid 8 USD for him last season. Paying about 7 to 9 USD is fair, but do not chase ESPN's rank of 64, since the experts see more downside than upside. He gives points, threes and a solid FT%, so pair him with players who bring rebounds, assists and blocks. Early in the season, check that he leads the Bulls in usage and that his three-point and free throw shooting has recovered from last season's late slump. Also watch for trade news before the 2027-03-04 deadline.
